set.prevailing_wage_basis: IB 538 Section IV.B states the City waives expedite program fees for 100% affordable housing projects (and for retail or commercial with 100% affordable housing on site); other eligible projects pay the expedite fee in IB-503. A waived fee is a form of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) (fees normally required that are waived or forgiven by a political subdivision), so the 100% affordable path can count toward public funding unless the subsidy is de minimis under 1720(c)(3) or another 1720(c) exemption applies. Mixed-income projects that pay the expedite fee receive processing priority only, which is not a 1720(b) form of public funds. https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletins/538 and https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: IB 538 reread. The Nov 9 note that projects pay all fees was wrong; expedite fees are waived for 100% affordable projects (standard fees and deposits still apply). Prevailing wage changed from false to unclear because the waiver is a 1720(b)(4) form of public funds whose weight depends on project size (de minimis test) and other 1720(c) exemptions.

reason: IB 538 waives expedite fees for 100% affordable projects; PW basis said no waiver

set.typical_award_size: Conduit private activity bonds sized to project debt. Enclave Montecito / Sol Vista (96 units, Otay Ranch Village 2): inducement up to $25 million (HA Resolution 2025-006, August 5, 2025), TEFRA hearing and bond issuance approval April 21, 2026 with an issuance amount not to exceed $14,000,000. Resolution 2024-103 (May 21, 2024) updated the Authority's conduit bond policies so the City is the issuer in most instances rather than JPAs; Master Fee Schedule Chapter 19 sets Housing Authority application, issuance and monitoring fees. Not every Chula Vista deal uses the Authority: Otay Ranch II (270 units, Rock Mountain Road and SR 125) received a $31,220,000 bond allocation on December 10, 2025 with the California Municipal Finance Authority as issuer, and the City's May 19, 2026 TEFRA approval for that project was for the CMFA issuance.
set.layering_notes: The 2024 policy makes the Housing Authority the default issuer, which keeps issuer fees local, but JPA issuance (CMFA for Otay Ranch II) still occurs; when a JPA issues, the City acts only as TEFRA host. Pairs with 4 percent LIHTC, City Low-Mod and LHTF loans and parkland fee waivers (separate records). Read on the City's eSCRIBE agenda portal; bond policy PDF not downloadable (403). Otay Ranch II issuer confirmed in the CTCAC/CDLAC staff report CA-25-798.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: removed Otay Ranch II as an Authority bond example. CTCAC staff report CA-25-798 (Dec 10, 2025) names the California Municipal Finance Authority as CDLAC applicant and bond issuer.

reason: Otay Ranch II was a CMFA issuance, not Housing Authority bonds

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. The 2025 Housing Element APR describes two layers. Housing Element Program 5 requires that 30% of homes in new subdivisions be 1,500 square feet or smaller and affordable to moderate and below income households, through deed restriction or an affordable housing plan approved by the Planning Commission or Council (size limits, rental units, second units); the Zoning Code was amended in 2009 to carry this out and 34 lots have been approved under it (none built yet). The same APR entry states that Municipal Code Section 17.80.220 requires 20% lower income units in developments. The code text was not available, so whether 17.80.220 is the 2009 implementing section or a separate requirement, and its unit thresholds, are not confirmed.
set.affordability_requirement: Per the 2025 APR: Program 5 targets moderate and below income (30% of subdivision homes, 1,500 square feet or smaller); Section 17.80.220 is described as requiring 20% lower income units. Confirm the code text before relying on either figure.
set.layering_notes: Functions as a light inclusionary rule with no in-lieu fee or fund found. Section 17.80.220 is not on the zoneomics mirror (Chapter 17.80 page loads without section text) and gocodebook returns 403; ask the Planning Department for the current section and whether the 30% size rule and the 20% lower income rule both apply.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: APR reread. The 30%/1,500 sq ft figure is the Housing Element Program 5 objective; the APR separately cites 17.80.220 as requiring 20% lower income units. Record now states both as the APR does; code text still unconfirmed.

reason: Reconcile 30% Program 5 objective with APR description of 17.80.220 (20% lower income)

set.layering_notes: Napa is one of the few California cities with a codified local bonus above the state maximum (to 100% total), which matters for small infill sites downtown and along the four General Plan corridor focus areas. AB 2334 (unlimited density and three extra stories for 100% affordable projects in Napa County, a very low vehicle travel area) applies by state law even before the local text is updated. :AH overlay sites in the Housing Element site inventory (including City owned sites under Program H2.F) carry the fee deferral and local fund incentives, which pair with the impact fee and TOT loans above. Density bonus alone does not trigger prevailing wage; City funds do. Code text read on the official ecode360 code (17.52.130 at ecode360.com/43397951; 17.36 at ecode360.com/43397139); the Housing Element PDF and 2023 APR were opened on cityofnapa.org.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: source moved from the zoneomics mirror to the official ecode360 code. 17.52.130 (O2010-3, O2011-2) confirms the supplemental density bonus to 100%, small project definition and 30-year agreement; 17.36.040 confirms priority processing and fee deferral to occupancy for :AH sites.

set.typical_award_size: HOME allocation FY 2024 $1,314,087.60 (down from $2,240,380 in FY 2010 and $1,067,408 in FY 2016); PLHA about $3,000,000 a year since 2019; together about $4,600,000 a year of recurring production money. City cash gap financing has averaged $6,000,000 per project on the last two developments (Finamore Place, completed February 2022, and Miraflores Apartments). The A-LHTF Build More Homes Initiative adds $5,000,000 of the initial $16,000,000 trust fund allocation. Anaheim also administers CDBG, ESG and HOPWA for the region.
set.layering_notes: Anaheim does not run a competitive NOFA; it assembles sites (Beach Boulevard corridor, former motels) and selects developers by RFP, then layers HOME, PLHA, A-LHTF and Housing Authority PBVs. The City is an HHAP direct recipient and a HOPWA grantee for Orange County, so operating subsidies for PSH can come from the same department. Stack order seen in practice: City land lease plus HOME or PLHA loan, Housing Authority PBVs, County MHSA/BHSA or OCHFT loan, 4% credits with CMFA or CSCDA bonds. Davis-Bacon on HOME projects of 12 or more assisted units; state prevailing wage on all City funds. Figures from the A-LHTF Guidelines (amended June 9, 2026), reopened Nov 10, 2026 on anaheim.net with a Chrome user agent. Project details from Pass 3 not reopened in the audit: Miraflores (85 PSH family units, 2024, 60-year ground lease, $3,000,000 HOME loan, 8 vouchers) and Center of Hope (72 PSH units, 2023, $2,000,000 City construction loan, 50 vouchers). anaheim.net HTML pages, Action Plan PDFs and CivicAlerts return 403.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: source PDF opened at anaheim.net/DocumentCenter/View/66427 (A-LHTF Guidelines, amended June 9, 2026) and confirms the HOME, PLHA, $4.6M and $6M average gap figures; restored to verified. set.typical_award_size: Fee-funded local gap loan fund. New fees adopted September 23, 2026 (Resolution 2026-202, adopting the June 30, 2026 EPS nexus study) and Ordinance 09-2026 (second reading October 14, 2026), effective January 1, 2027, replacing the 2013 per-unit fees ($6,396 per single or two-unit dwelling and $3,837 per multi-unit dwelling in 2025): residential $3.59 per square foot single-unit, $3.29 owner-occupied multi-unit and $1.46 renter-occupied multi-unit; nonresidential $2.15 shopping center, $2.29 office (was $0.00), $0.39 industrial (manufacturing and warehouse merged), $1,146.75 per hotel room, plus per-unit rates for other uses, all including the 3% administrative fee. Fees were set at roughly 7.5% of the maximum justifiable fee. The City releases an RFP when the fund balance can support a project (generally about $5 million); the City reports $84 million lent to sixteen projects since inception (developer page, not opened).
set.affordability_requirement: Ordinance 09-2026 expands fund uses to very low, low and moderate income households (previously very low and low) and adds EGMC 16.88.080 authorizing a local preference policy for deed-restricted rental and ownership units, consistent with fair housing law. Deed-restricted affordable housing is exempt from the residential fee.
set.next_deadline: New fee schedule effective January 1, 2027. No open RFP found as of 2026-11-10; watch elkgrove.gov/affordable-housing/developers and the City's purchasing RFP page. Contact Joshua Tovar, Management Analyst, jtovar@elkgrove.gov, or the Housing and Public Services Division, (916) 683-7111.
set.layering_notes: Elk Grove is an impact-fee jurisdiction (like the City and County of Sacramento) with no inclusionary option, so market-rate rental projects pay the fee rather than build units; the 2026 renter-occupied rate was deliberately set low ($1.46 per square foot recommended) because the nexus study found multifamily infeasible at higher fees. Elk Grove is outside the SHRA lending area (SHRA finances in other cities only under cooperation agreements), so this fund, state sources and Elk Grove's own PLHA are the local layer. Past RFPs tied fund loans to City-owned sites (Sheldon Farms North and Old Town, 2023). elkgrove.gov HTML pages and codepublishing.com return 403 to automated access, but council attachment PDFs open; facts here come from the Sept 23, 2026 staff report (item 8.2), Ordinance 09-2026 (Oct 14, 2026 item 7.5) and the Sept 23 and Oct 14 minutes. The North State BIA supported the staff recommendation at the hearing.
set.audit_note: Follow-up Nov 10, 2026: hearing outcome confirmed. Sept 23 minutes: Ordinance 09-2026 introduced 4-0 (Suen absent) and Resolution 2026-202 adopted at staff-recommended rates; Oct 14 minutes: Ordinance 09-2026 adopted on second reading. Fees effective Jan 1, 2027.
